3. Reachable-set controllers and MPC

Read a closed-loop policy trace

Ready · analytic illustration

Separate predicted stage coordinates from observed execution state and label the observation update. A deterministic replay is one trajectory. It is not full forward reachability or a nonlinear enclosure.

Mathematical input

Two observed updates
kobserved x[k]u[k]=1−x[k]predicted and observed x[k+1]
0011
1101

Reproduce this result

Full input description and JSON

Discrete plant x[k+1]=x[k]+u[k]. At each of two updates, observe x[k], choose u[k]=1-x[k], predict one stage, apply the action, and observe the new state.

Open the structured chapter manifest JSON

Command

python3 scripts/reports/learning_closed_loop_toy.py

Expected output

update=0 observation=0 action=1 prediction_end=1 plant_state=1
update=1 observation=1 action=0 prediction_end=1 plant_state=1

Intermediate geometry. At each update, the one-stage prediction endpoint matches the observed plant state. The trace is one policy-conditioned path in a scalar state coordinate.

Support limits. This dependency-free discrete example illustrates observation and action timing. It does not invoke a CSL controller or establish full reachability, feasibility for other states, or an enclosure.
